title_en: 274: How Tokenized Cash Is Modernizing Money, Markets and Investing
title_zh: 274：代币化现金如何革新货币、市场与投资 — Becky Milcham（BlackRock）
subtitle_zh: BlackRock 的 Becky Milcham 谈代币化现金与数字钱包如何重塑资金流动。
summary_zh: 本期 The Bid 由 Oscar Pulido 对话 BlackRock 全球现金分销主管兼国际现金管理业务负责人 Becky Milcham（节目中被戏称现金女王），主题是代币化现金（tokenized cash）如何成为代币化（tokenization）最具说服力的现实应用之一。Milcham 首先祛魅：代币化不是一种新资产，而是给传统现金类工具套上一层区块链上的技术外壳（wrapper）——底层还是银行存款或货币市场基金，只是数字化之后能做过去做不到的事。她把加密资产（cryptocurrency）、稳定币（stablecoin）、代币化现金三者区分开：加密货币价值仅由链上供需决定、波动剧烈；稳定币由一池储备资产（reserve asset）支撑，美国的 GENIUS 法案（Genius Act）对支付型稳定币的储备有明确界定，功能上接近口袋里的现金；而代币化现金——包括代币化存款（tokenized deposit）与代币化货币市场基金——因为底层就是可产生收益的现金工具，所以能带 yield。她用从书信到电子邮件的类比说明即时性才是核心变化：过去一笔跨境结算要几小时甚至几天，代币化后现金不再闲置，结算更快、透明度更高、摩擦更少。Milcham 认为推动这一变化的三方面因素是技术进步、监管出台（尤其美国）与传统企业开始把它纳入日常财资管理系统（treasury management system），并特别提到代理式工作流（agentic workflow）与智能合约（smart contract）：预先写好规则，满足条件即自动完成一笔资金转移。谈到数字钱包（digital wallet），她认为现金天然站在生态最前沿——投资任何东西都得先有现金。她给出三个未来信号：普及程度（尤其是超越 DeFi 圈层）、互操作性（interoperability）、以及全球监管如何真正落地。整体是一堂把代币化从概念讲回金融基础设施的入门课。
description: 274: How Tokenized Cash Is Modernizing Money, Markets and Investing

turns.en: When most investors think about innovation in financial markets, they tend to focus on the assets themselves, stocks, bonds, cryptocurrencies, or increasingly private markets.
turns.zh: 当大多数投资者想到金融市场的创新时，他们往往聚焦于资产本身——股票、债券、加密货币（cryptocurrency），以及越来越多的私募市场（private market）。

turns.en: But some of the biggest changes are happening behind the scenes, in the infrastructure that allows money and investments to move around the world.
turns.zh: 但一些最大的变革正发生在幕后，发生在让资金和投资得以在全球流转的基础设施之中。

turns.en: And as markets become more digital, many believe that the way cash moves, settles and acts as collateral, could be on the verge of its biggest transformation in decades.
turns.zh: 随着市场日益数字化，许多人认为，现金的流转、结算以及充当抵押品（collateral）的方式，可能正迎来数十年来最大的一次转型。

turns.en: We've seen adoption across the DeFi community, but what we're starting to see is more traditional use cases, where people are leveraging the technology to make themselves faster and more efficient.
turns.zh: 我们已经在 DeFi（去中心化金融）社区看到了应用落地，但如今我们开始看到的是更传统的应用场景，人们正借助这项技术让自己变得更快、更高效。

turns.en: And one of those use cases is to transmit money around the world and faster payments. So what could that mean for investors? Welcome to The Bit, where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance.
turns.zh: 而其中一个应用场景，就是在全球汇划资金、加快支付。那么这对投资者意味着什么？欢迎收听 The Bid，在这档节目里，我们拆解市场正在发生什么，也探索那些改变经济与金融的力量。

turns.en: I'm Oscar Pulido. Joining me today is someone who's been at the center of these changes. Becky Milcham is global head of cash distribution and head of the international cash management business at BlackRock.
turns.zh: 我是 Oscar Pulido。今天来到节目的，是一位一直处于这些变革中心的人物——Becky Milcham，她是 BlackRock 的全球现金分销主管兼国际现金管理业务负责人。

turns.en: Becky has joined us on The Bit before to help explain why cash matters in an investment portfolio. Today, she's back to discuss why cash is becoming one of the most compelling real-world applications of tokenization, how new digital infrastructure could reshape the movement of money through financial markets, and why understanding these changes may become increasingly important for investors.
turns.zh: Becky 此前曾做客 The Bid，帮我们解读现金为何在投资组合中如此重要。今天她再次来到节目，讨论现金为何正成为代币化（tokenization）最具说服力的现实应用之一、新的数字基础设施如何重塑资金在金融市场中的流动，以及为何理解这些变革对投资者会愈发重要。

turns.en: Becky, thank you so much for joining us on The Bit. It's great to be here, Oscar, and to be in the New York studio for the first time. Yes, we usually talk via video.
turns.zh: Becky，非常感谢你再次做客 The Bid。很高兴来到这里，Oscar，也是我第一次来到纽约演播室。是啊，我们平时都是隔着视频连线聊的。

turns.en: You're in London normally. I'm in New York, but it's great to have you here in person. The last time that we spoke was back in 2024 when we have you on.
turns.zh: 你平时在伦敦，我在纽约，但能这样当面请到真是太好了。我们上一次对话还要追溯到 2024 年你上节目的时候。

turns.en: We're usually talking about this topic of cash. In fact, we've used the title Queen of Cash. This is an area of expertise for you. Back when we last spoke, tokenization felt like an interesting idea and a topic that was nascent.
turns.zh: 我们当时聊的通常就是现金这个主题，事实上我们还用过『现金女王』（Queen of Cash）这个头衔，这确实是你的专长领域。我们上次对话那会儿，代币化还只是一个有趣的概念、一个刚刚萌芽的话题。

turns.en: We've recently spoken to Rob Goldstein, BlackRock's chief operating officer, and he's helped us understand a little bit more about tokenization and what it really is.
turns.zh: 我们最近采访了 Rob Goldstein——BlackRock 的首席运营官（COO），他帮我们更深入地理解了代币化究竟是什么。

turns.en: They were also hearing about the concept of tokenized money market funds, stable coins, and digital cash. There's a lot of new terminology that we're having to learn.
turns.zh: 我们也在那里听到了代币化货币市场基金（tokenized money market fund）、稳定币（stablecoin）和数字现金这些概念。有太多新术语等着我们去学习。

turns.en: Before we get into what's changed since we last spoke to you, can you explain what is tokenized cash? I think the concept of tokenization can be a little bit confusing.
turns.zh: 在我们聊自上次对话以来都有哪些变化之前，你能先解释一下什么是代币化现金吗？我想代币化这个概念可能会让人有点困惑。

turns.en: A lot of people think it's a new type of product, but the way I describe it is it's just putting a technology wrapper around a traditional asset class.
turns.zh: 很多人以为它是一种全新的产品，但我的描述是：它只是给一类传统资产套上了一层技术的『外壳』（wrapper）。

turns.en: What that essentially means is that you've got different types of cash today, and in this new world, you can have them digitally represented on a blockchain.
turns.zh: 这本质上意味着，如今有不同种类的现金，在这个新世界里，你可以把它们以数字化的形式呈现在区块链（blockchain）上。

turns.en: As you've mentioned, I think most people are familiar with stable coins today, but you've got this emerging set of traditional forms of cash, such as tokenized deposits, like a bank deposit, a bit of a tokenized wrapper, money market funds available with that tokenized wrapper as well.
turns.zh: 正如你提到的，我想如今大多数人都熟悉稳定币了，但还有一批正在兴起、源于传统形态的现金，比如代币化存款（tokenized deposit），像银行存款那样，套上一层代币化的外壳；货币市场基金同样也可以加上这层代币化外壳。

turns.en: I think the important thing to remember here is that these are the same things underneath. It's just that digital wrapper that's wrapping around it to effectively mean it can do different things than it used to be able to do.
turns.zh: 我想这里最需要记住的一点是，它们的底层其实是完全相同的东西，只是外面套了那层数字外壳，从而让它们能做过去做不到的事情。

turns.en: That sounds familiar with what Rob had mentioned when we spoke to him, which is the types of assets you own are the same, but the way in which you own them is what's different.
turns.zh: 这听起来跟 Rob 在接受我们采访时说的很一致——你持有的资产类型是一样的，不一样的只是你持有它们的方式。

turns.en: I think that's what you're explaining with tokenization, and that can apply to cash as well. When people hear blockchain or tokenization, I think it's fair to say they immediately think about crypto.
turns.zh: 我觉得这正是你在解释代币化时所传达的意思，而且它同样适用于现金。当人们听到区块链或代币化时，坦率说，他们第一反应往往就是加密资产。

turns.en: Help me understand what's the difference between cryptocurrencies, stable coins, and tokenized cash. A cryptocurrency is a type of digital asset.
turns.zh: 帮我理解一下加密货币、稳定币和代币化现金之间有什么区别？加密货币是一种数字资产。

turns.en: It can be used as a form of payment, and that's how it has traditionally been adopted. But its value is driven simply by supply and demand on the blockchain, which means it can be quite volatile in terms of where that value goes to.
turns.zh: 它可以被用作一种支付手段，这也是它传统上被采用的方式。但它的价值仅仅由区块链上的供需决定，这意味着它的价值波动可能相当剧烈。

turns.en: What you've seen as a result is an emergence of stable coins, which designed to maintain a relatively stable value. They are backed by a pool of reserve assets, and payment stable coins under some of the regulations that have come out, such as the Genius Act in the United States, have to be backed by a very defined pool of reserve assets.
turns.zh: 由此带来的结果，是稳定币的兴起，它们被设计用来维持相对稳定的价值。它们由一池储备资产（reserve asset）作为支撑；而根据已经出台的一些监管规则，比如美国的《GENIUS 法案》（Genius Act），支付型稳定币必须有一组界定非常清晰的储备资产来支撑。

turns.en: They enable you to move money, make payments. It's a store of value and a medium of exchange through the blockchain. I like to think of stable coins as being quite synonymous to the cash in your pocket.
turns.zh: 它们让你能够转账、支付，是借助区块链实现的价值储存手段和交换媒介。我喜欢把稳定币理解成和你口袋里的现金几乎是一回事。

turns.en: Then you've got tokenized cash, which, as I mentioned before, can be tokenized deposits, a bank deposit, simply with that tokenized wrapper, and tokenized money market funds.
turns.zh: 然后就是代币化现金，正如我之前所说，它可以是代币化存款——就是一笔银行存款，只不过套上了那层代币化外壳——也可以是代币化货币市场基金。

turns.en: The distinction here is that stable coins can't pay a return, whereas you have traditional cash investment tools, just bank deposits, and money market funds with their tokenized wrapper that can have that return aspect, that yield aspect on them.
turns.zh: 这里的区别在于，稳定币不能支付回报；而代币化现金用的是传统的现金投资工具——就是银行存款和货币市场基金加上它们的代币化外壳——这些是可以带有回报、带有收益（yield）属性的。

turns.en: Today, for example, normally when I'm in the States, carry some dollars in my pocket to perhaps tip or something, the stable coin is simply doing that in the digital form.
turns.zh: 比如说今天，我在美国时通常会往口袋里装些美元，用来给个小费之类，稳定币所做的，就是以数字化的形式完成这件事。

turns.en: I wouldn't ordinarily keep too much cash in my pockets because it's not going to earn me anything there. I would then put it into my bank account or put it into a money market fund where I can earn a return on that.
turns.zh: 我一般不会在口袋里放太多现金，因为放在那儿一分钱也生不出来。我会把它存进银行账户，或者放进货币市场基金，让它可以赚得回报。

turns.en: One thing I've been likening this to is, if you think about some of the traditional forms of communication back in the day, we would have received a letter in the post and we went through a huge transformation when we moved to a world of email and instantaneous receipt of communications.
turns.zh: 我一直把这件事比作通信方式的变迁：想想过去那些传统的通信方式，我们原本要等一封信寄到手，而当我们进入电子邮件、能够即时收到信息的时代时，我们经历了一场巨大的变革。

turns.en: That's again what this technology wrapper enables you to do on the blockchain. It's that instantaneous form of payment rather than receiving something in the post.
turns.zh: 而这项技术外壳在区块链上所能实现的，正是同样的效果——它是一种即时的支付形式，而不再像等邮递那样慢慢收东西。

turns.en: I remember the days for birthdays and Christmas when my relatives, perhaps my grandmother, might have sent me 10 pounds in the post and a couple of days later, I'd have received, hopefully, received it.
turns.zh: 我记得以前过生日和圣诞节那会儿，家里亲戚、也许是外婆，会给我寄上 10 英镑，几天之后我才收到——但愿能收到吧。

turns.en: Essentially, what we're doing in the world of tokenization is enabling that instantaneous movement of cash. Well, I can still think of when you go and buy somebody a birthday card or a graduation card.
turns.zh: 所以说到底，我们在代币化世界里所做的，就是让现金的这种即时流转成为可能。——不过我还是会想到，你去给别人买生日贺卡或者毕业贺卡的情景。

turns.en: The cards are money holders where people drop physical cash in there. That's how the card is structured. We're talking about something really basic, which is just payments and medium of exchange.
turns.zh: 那些贺卡其实就是放钱的，人们把现金塞进去，贺卡就是这么设计的。我们谈的其实是很基本的事情——就是支付和交换媒介。

turns.en: For years, it has been something physical that you exchange, a piece of paper, whether it's dollars or pound sterling, maybe when you're back in London.
turns.zh: 多年来，它所交换的一直是实体的东西，一张纸，不管是美元还是英镑——也许你回伦敦的时候用的就是英镑。

turns.en: What you're highlighting is that this is a modernizing space. You mentioned cryptocurrencies, which is one way of doing payment, but there's volatility associated with that, something like Bitcoin, for example.
turns.zh: 你强调的这一点是，这是一个正在现代化的领域。你提到了加密货币，那是支付的一种方式，但它伴随着波动性，比如比特币。

turns.en: You mentioned stable coins and tokenized cash, perhaps having more stability, but also being digital in how they're used. Becky, why is all of this moving from concept to reality?
turns.zh: 你还提到了稳定币和代币化现金，它们也许更稳定，而且在使用方式上也实现了数字化。Becky，为什么这一切正从概念走向现实？过去几年究竟发生了什么变化，才让我们此时此刻要来聊这个话题？

turns.en: What's changed over the last couple of years that is causing us to have this conversation right now? I think about in three areas, really. There's been huge advancement in the technology, and we're starting to see that greater adoption in technology and the use of the blockchain.
turns.zh: 我觉得主要在三个方面。首先是技术上取得了巨大进步，我们开始看到这项技术和区块链得到更广泛的应用。

turns.en: I think one of the things that really propelled it, and probably since the last time we spoke, was some of the rules that are coming out from governments.
turns.zh: 我想，真正推动它的一件事——大概也是从我们上次对话之后开始的——就是各国政府开始出台的一些规则。

turns.en: When you start to get some regulations in this space, that starts to bring more comfort and trust in the space. You start to see more adoption through that.
turns.zh: 当这个领域开始有了一些监管，人们就会对这个领域感到更踏实、更信任，你也会由此看到更多的应用落地。

turns.en: We've got around the world now a swathe of regulations looking at this space and looking particularly at the rules governing how stable coins work today, how tokenized assets work today.
turns.zh: 如今全球有一大批监管都在审视这个领域，尤其聚焦于治理当下稳定币如何运作、代币化资产如何运作的规则。

turns.en: This, for me, has really come to life a little bit more this year, is that we're starting to see real-the-world uses of the technology. As we've mentioned, it makes things faster, it makes things more efficient, and there's been a lot of talk around that.
turns.zh: 对我来说，今年这件事真正开始变得鲜活起来，是因为我们开始看到这项技术在现实世界中的应用。正如我们所说，它让事情更快、更高效，这方面的讨论也特别多。

turns.en: What I'm starting to hear in my job is actually some of those use cases coming across. This is perhaps corporates around the world that are in more of a traditional finance world.
turns.zh: 在我的工作里，我开始听到那些应用场景真正落地——这大概是全球那些身处更传统金融世界的企业。

turns.en: We've clearly seen adoption across the DeFi community, but what we're starting to see is some of the more traditional use cases where people are leveraging the technology to make themselves faster and more efficient.
turns.zh: 我们在 DeFi 社区确实已经看到大量应用，但我们开始看到的，是更传统的一些应用场景，人们借助这项技术让自己更快、更高效。其中的一个应用场景，同样是在全球汇划资金和加快支付。

turns.en: One of those use cases, again, is to transmit money around the world and faster payments. Can you talk maybe a more of an example? You say traditional corporate, so would this be a corporation that is managing cash on their balance sheet and the way they're doing that is modernizing?
turns.zh: 你能不能多讲一个例子？你说的传统企业，是指一家在管理自己资产负债表上现金、并且正用现代化方式来做这件事的公司吗？

turns.en: Yeah. I think they're starting to realize the benefits of how efficient technology can make them and adopting that blockchain into their day-to-day systems and upgrading what would have been traditional treasury management systems.
turns.zh: 是的。我想他们开始意识到高效的技术能为他们带来多少好处，于是把区块链纳入日常系统，并升级原本传统的资金管理系统（treasury management system）。

turns.en: You mentioned technology, you mentioned regulation, and you've talked a little bit about the infrastructure seems to be changing as well. I don't think most investors spend much time thinking about how trades settle and how payments move through the plumbing of the financial system, but help me understand what actually is not working today that is why tokenized cash is maybe going to benefit markets and
turns.zh: 你谈了技术，谈了监管，也略微提到了基础设施似乎也在改变。我想大多数投资者不会花太多时间去琢磨交易如何结算、支付如何在金融体系的『管道』里流转。但帮我理解一下——今天究竟是什么地方在出问题，才让代币化现金或许能惠及市场和

turns.en: investors. Yeah. Technology is overhauling really a lot of the financial markets ecosystem. I often refer to the cash team as plumbing experts because we get to see and get to see all the movements behind the scene of where cash moves and what can go wrong and things do go wrong today.
turns.zh: 投资者？是的。技术正在真正革新金融市场生态系统的很大一部分。我常把现金团队称作『管道专家』，因为我们能看到现金流动的幕后——各种动向，哪里会出问题；而如今问题确实会发生。

turns.en: You've got multiple systems that are not designed to work together and where I think in our regular day-to-day lives, we're becoming more used to that digital experience and everything being instantaneous and available to us.
turns.zh: 现在有好多系统，当初并不是设计成能协同工作的。而我觉得，在我们日常的生活里，我们已经越来越习惯那种数字化的体验，习惯一切都能即时、随时可得。

turns.en: Even the scenes that plumbing for payments in particular isn't that efficient today, and it can take hours, sometimes days, to settle transactions, and that's really where the technology is going to help things like cash not just sit idle, it's going to enable that faster settlement, that transparency, and for all intents and purposes, making things more frictionless through the ecosystem.
turns.zh: 特别是在支付这个环节，所谓的『管道』如今其实并不高效，一笔交易结算可能要花上几个小时、有时甚至是几天。而这正是这项技术能发挥作用的地方——让现金这样的东西不再只是闲置。它将实现更快的结算、更高的透明度，并且在实质上让整个生态系统里的运作都变得更加顺畅、更少摩擦。

turns.en: Right. Talk a little bit more about that. I'm starting to highlight what starts to change if the payment system continues to modernize because it's already starting to modernize, and what does tokenized cash actually improve in terms of how markets function?
turns.zh: 好。再多讲讲这块吧。我想强调的是，如果支付体系持续现代化——因为它其实已经开始了现代化——究竟哪些东西会开始改变？而代币化现金在『市场如何运转』这件事上，到底改进了什么？

turns.en: When I think about the improvements and what they're actually going to mean, you can move money faster. You can have platforms around the world moving things seamlessly between each other, and I'm taking you back to that kind of example of the corporate that I mentioned.
turns.zh: 当我思考这些改进以及它们真正的意义时，你会想到：你可以更快地转账，可以让全球各地的平台之间无缝地流转资金。我又要带你回到我提到的那类企业的例子。

turns.en: This means that you can do around the clock, cross-border payments, and a world that could be more 24-7, 365 days a year. The bit that really brings this all together is that once you've got something in that technology wrapper, it means that you can tell it what to do.
turns.zh: 这意味着你可以全天候、24/7、一年 365 天地进行跨境支付。而真正把这一切串起来的关键在于：一旦某样东西被装进了那层技术外壳，就意味着你可以给它下达指令、告诉它该做什么。

turns.en: You can program it, and if we think about the ability to then use things like AI and that ability to use agentic workflows, you can have something that can be automated through that.
turns.zh: 你可以对它进行编程，而如果考虑到之后运用 AI、运用智能体工作流（agentic workflow）的能力，你就可以让某些流程借此实现自动化。

turns.en: So in the example of a smart contract around a money movement, you can have something that is literally programmed once a set of criteria is met to make that movement.
turns.zh: 以围绕一笔资金转移的智能合约（smart contract）为例，你可以事先编写好规则，一旦满足某组条件，它就自动完成那笔转账。

turns.en: You don't have to have that manual intervention. That makes a company more efficient in terms of how it is managing its cash, or making payments to its suppliers, or perhaps making investments.
turns.zh: 你不必再有人工介入。这让一家公司在管理自身现金、向供应商付款、或者进行投资时，都变得更加高效。

turns.en: The fact that you're mentioning that this is where you can apply AI is not something I had considered, but you're saying that the technology that is being created is going to improve the ability for that corporation to manage its cash on its balance sheet.
turns.zh: 你提到这是可以应用 AI 的地方——这一点我此前还真没想过。你的意思是，正在被创造出来的这项技术，将会提升那家公司管理其资产负债表上现金的能力。

turns.en: Yeah, and it can make things much more instantaneous. And the fact that you've then got that immediate movement, that immediate transition of a payment and a settlement, that you can have a more efficient hold on your work in capital, essentially.
turns.zh: 是的，而且它能让一切变得更即时。你由此获得了即时转移——一笔支付和结算的即时完成——说到底是让你能更高效地占用和运用你的营运资本（working capital）。

turns.en: And what that means for cash is that you can then have a better grip on where it is, and you can be more efficient with the investments that you make.
turns.zh: 这对现金的意义在于：你能更好地掌握它所在的位置，并且能更高效地安排你所做的投资。

turns.en: And so in the world of tokenization, it means that you can move very seamlessly from something such as a stablecoin, which isn't going to earn you any yield, into something like a tokenized money market fund, which has all the benefits of the traditional money market funds and they have today, but just in that tokenized form.
turns.zh: 所以在代币化的世界里，这意味着你可以非常顺畅地从稳定币——那种不会给你带来任何收益的东西——切换到代币化货币市场基金，后者拥有传统货币市场基金今天所具备的一切优势，只不过是以代币化的形式存在。而且这一切都能即时完成。

turns.en: And that can all happen instantaneously. Becky, I want to come back to the discussion I had with Rob Goldstein, BlackRock's Chief Operating Officer.
turns.zh: Becky，我想回到我和 BlackRock 首席运营官 Rob Goldstein 的那次讨论。

turns.en: And we started to talk about digital wallets, and in fact, he gave some personal anecdotes about how maybe the younger members of his family who are now entering financial markets would be most likely to own their assets in a digital wallet as opposed to the traditional financial system.
turns.zh: 我们开始聊到数字钱包（digital wallet）。事实上，他还讲了一些个人的趣事，说也许他家里那些刚步入金融市场的年轻一辈，最可能把资产放在数字钱包里，而不是放在传统金融体系里。

turns.en: My mom, I don't think is going to have a digital wallet anytime soon. That said, my kids may want everything in a digital wallet. Part of it is age, part of it is tech fluency, part of it is starting point.
turns.zh: 我妈妈呢，我想她短期内是不会用数字钱包的。话虽如此，我的孩子们也许会希望把一切都放进数字钱包。这部分是年龄，部分是技术熟练度，部分是各自的起点。

turns.en: It goes back to access, it goes back to your phone. If you think about your phone in the year 2030, do you have more or less apps on the phone?
turns.zh: 这归根结底取决于可得性，取决于你的手机。想想 2030 年的手机——到那时你手机上的应用是变多了还是变少了？

turns.en: And if you believe that the apps you have are going to have to do more things, the token and blockchain and the related technologies are important enablers in being able to do that.
turns.zh: 如果你相信你所拥有的应用得承担更多功能，那么代币、区块链以及相关技术，就是实现这一点的重要使能因素。

turns.en: There will be an app that will be the ability to move money around, to do investments, to build portfolios. Whether or not you even know that you just bought a token of a fund or you just bought a token of a stock, that's effectively what will enable that fewer app environment that we're describing.
turns.zh: 会有那么一个应用，让你能够转账、投资、构建投资组合。甚至无论你是否意识到自己刚刚买的是一枚基金份额的代币、还是一只股票的代币——这实际上就是我们所说的那个『更少应用』的环境得以成立的关键。

turns.en: What are you seeing in terms of the adoption of digital wallets and where is cash maybe playing a leading role in those wallets? Yeah, and a digital wallet is a key part of the new ecosystem that we're talking about.
turns.zh: 你在数字钱包普及这方面看到了什么？现金又是否可能在这些钱包里扮演引领性的角色？是啊，数字钱包是我们所说的这个新生态中的关键一环。

turns.en: You have to have it if you want to operate on the blockchain. And one of the reasons that cash is at the forefront of all of this is because you need cash to invest in anything.
turns.zh: 如果你想在区块链上操作，你就必须拥有它。而现金之所以能站在这一切的前沿，一个原因就是：你要投资任何东西都得先有现金。

turns.en: And so it has been adopted largely for the use of digital payments today, but you're then seeing that need from a client wanting to have cash, wanting to earn an investment yield on that.
turns.zh: 所以如今它主要在数字支付这一用途上被采用；但接下来你会看到这样一种来自客户的需求——他们想持有现金，又想在这之上赚取投资收益。

turns.en: They're being demand for traditional instruments like money market funds. And then there's a future world where we will see much more in terms of our assets wrapped in that tokenized wrapper, that digital wrapper, and available through your digital wallet.
turns.zh: 市场对货币市场基金这类传统工具是有需求的。而未来的世界里，我们会看到更多的资产被裹上那层代币化、数字化的外壳，并通过你的数字钱包来触达。

turns.en: But you have to start somewhere and because cash is needed as an asset class everywhere, cash is the natural progression from that stablecoin, that form of actual cash, into something like a tokenized money market fund where you can earn a yield.
turns.zh: 但万事总得从一个地方起步。正因为现金作为一类资产在处处都被需要，现金便成为一条自然演进的路线——从稳定币这种实际现金的形态，走向代币化货币市场基金，在那里你可以赚取收益。

turns.en: Becky, when we think about these trends that you're seeing, the adoption of digital assets, digital wallets, tokenized cash, is this something that is taking place globally all at the same time or are there particular regions that are leading on this?
turns.zh: Becky，当我们思考你观察到的这些趋势——数字资产、数字钱包、代币化现金的普及——这是全球同步发生的事情，还是有某些地区走在前面？

turns.en: Well, as I think about the adoption to date, a lot of the adoption of stablecoins has been in dollar denominated stablecoins. And I think some of the rules and regulations that have come out to clarify that have helped that.
turns.zh: 就目前普及的情况来看，稳定币的大量采用集中在以美元计价的稳定币上。我想，已经出台的一些旨在澄清相关问题的规则与监管，对这一点也有所帮助。

turns.en: We are seeing demand across the world from some of our investors. And again, back to the more kind of traditional investors that we have around the world than some of our corporate clients, they're thinking about this in terms of how they can adopt an overhaul entire systems.
turns.zh: 我们正看到来自全球一些投资者的需求。再说回我们遍布全球的、更偏传统的那类投资者以及企业客户，他们思考的角度是：自己该如何采用、甚至彻底改造一整套系统。

turns.en: And so naturally, you need something available in every single currency, but we haven't got all of the rules and regulations finalized around the world for what stablecoins are going to need to look like in terms of their reserve assets that back them.
turns.zh: 所以很自然地，你需要一种在每一种货币下都能获得的工具；但全球范围内，关于稳定币用来支撑自身的储备资产应当具备什么样的形态，相关的规则与监管还远未全部敲定。

turns.en: And so we're starting to see that come out. And naturally, in the same way that we would have a digital form of cash in every currency, we're going to naturally want some yield bearing solutions in every form of currency.
turns.zh: 所以我们正看到这些逐步出台。而很自然地，正如我们要为每一种货币都提供现金的数字化形态一样，我们也一定会希望在每一种货币下都能有一些能带来收益的解决方案。

turns.en: You see those today in, again, the more traditional wrappers that we have, like traditional money market funds, are available in lots of different currencies.
turns.zh: 你今天就能看到这些——同样地，在我们那些更传统的外壳下，比如传统的货币市场基金，就已经支持许多不同的货币。那么自然而然，下一步就是让这些工具以代币化的形态出现。

turns.en: And then so naturally, the next step is to have those available in tokenized form. So Becky, we're still clearly in the early development of tokenized assets.
turns.zh: 所以，Becky，我们显然还处于代币化资产的早期发展阶段。我们正在讨论这个话题，而且今后看来还会讨论得更多。

turns.en: We're talking about this and it seems like we're going to be talking about it more going forward. But what would you be watching over the next few years to know whether this is really becoming part of mainstream finance and what do investors need to consider about this trend?
turns.zh: 那么在接下来的几年里，你会关注哪些信号，来判断这是否真的正在融入主流金融？而投资者又需要对这一趋势思考些什么？

turns.en: So I think clearly adoption is one thing. We're starting to see this growing ecosystem of digital cash. So our people using it is that growing beyond that DeFi ecosystem that we see today.
turns.zh: 我想，普及程度显然是一方面。我们正在看到一个不断成长的数字现金生态。使用它的人群是否在壮大，是否已经超越了当今我们看到的那个 DeFi 生态。

turns.en: I think the second thing is that interoperability and really proving that out can all these different technology systems work together. And I think the third thing, as I mentioned before, is really how we bed down the rules around the world on this, how regulation gets formed across the world.
turns.zh: 第二方面，我认为是互操作性（interoperability），真正去验证所有这些不同的技术系统能否协同工作。而第三方面，正如我之前所说，是我们在全球范围内如何把这些规则真正落实下来、监管如何在全球成形。

turns.en: Largely today, a lot of the stablecoins operate are in dollars, but we're starting to see emerging regulations around the world and different currency products coming to market.
turns.zh: 如今大部分在运营的稳定币都是以美元计价，但我们开始看到全球各地不断涌现的监管，以及不同货币的相应产品陆续进入市场。

turns.en: This isn't a new asset class, as I said before. It's simply modernizing the ecosystem that we have around us today and providing these digital rails to allow money to move.
turns.zh: 正如我之前所说，这不是一类新的资产。它只是对我们今天身处其中的这个生态进行现代化，并提供这些数字化的『铁轨』（digital rails），让资金得以流动。

turns.en: And I think the test for me, and coming back to an analogy I made earlier about receiving money from perhaps a grandparent in the post, I think the real test for me is when we see maybe my dad, because my grandmother is no longer with us sadly, but maybe my dad's sends me a tokenized money market fund for Christmas.
turns.zh: 而对我来说，检验的标志——回到我之前那个关于从长辈那里通过邮递收到钱的比喻——我想真正的检验时刻，是当我们看到也许我父亲——因为很遗憾我外婆已经不在了——也许是父亲，在圣诞节时给我发来一笔代币化货币市场基金。

turns.en: Well, I'm not sure how many kids will understand that gift right now, but maybe in the future they will. I'm actually remembering back when I was a kid, I don't know if you did this, Becky, but when I would travel, I would collect the physical currency of various countries and store it in a book.
turns.zh: 嗯，我不敢确定现在有多少孩子能懂这份礼物，但也许将来他们会懂的。说到这个，我倒是想起我小时候的事，不知道你有没有过这种经历，Becky——我每次出国旅行，都会收集各国的实体纸币，把它们夹进一本册子里保存。

turns.en: And I'm wondering if I need to start doing that again, just because some of these might go out of circulation at some point. I still have a glass jar with lots of different colorful notes from around the world.
turns.zh: 我甚至在想，是不是该重新做这件事了——因为这些纸币里，有的说不定哪天就退出流通了。我到现在还留着一个小玻璃罐，里面装着来自世界各地、各种花花绿绿的钞票。

turns.en: I wasn't the only person that was doing that. Becky, I mentioned at the beginning that you are the Queen of Cash. This is a topic that you have come and talked to us about.
turns.zh: 我想这么做的不止我一个人吧。Becky，节目一开始我说过你是『现金女王』，这也是你几度来和我们聊过的话题。

turns.en: You also mentioned that your team is known as plumbing experts. I'm going to stick with Queen of Cash as the title that we will bestow upon you.
turns.zh: 你还提到，你的团队被称为『管道专家』。不过我还是打算继续用『现金女王』作为授予你的头衔。

turns.en: Thanks for kind of taking us into this somewhat discreet part of the market and telling us about the modernization that is going on. And thanks for doing it here on The Bid.
turns.zh: 谢谢你带我们走进市场里这个颇为低调的角落，告诉我们这场正在进行的现代化。也谢谢你来到 The Bid 与我们分享这些。

turns.en: Thank you. Thanks for listening to this episode of The Bid. If you've enjoyed this episode, check out my discussion with BlackRock COO Rob Goldstein, where we explore how tokenization could revolutionize the finance industry.
turns.zh: 谢谢你。感谢你收听本期 The Bid。如果你喜欢这一期节目，也去看看我和 BlackRock 首席运营官 Rob Goldstein 的对话，我们一起探讨了代币化如何可能革新金融行业。
